title: Komodo, the Island of Dragons
passage: Komodo, the Island of Dragons. In between the Flores Sea and the Indian Ocean, there is a tiny island filled with dragons. It is called Komodo Island, and people from all over the world visit it to see the ancient animal that exists there. The Komodo dragon is in fact not a dragon at all. It is the world's largest lizard. They can grow up to three yards long and weigh about 90 kilograms. They use their tails and sharp teeth to hunt deer and pigs. When Komodo dragons bite an animal, they put poison into its blood. This hurts the animal slowly until it dies. They seldom attack humans, but if you ever see a Komodo dragon, you should still be afraid to get near it. Komodo Island has much more than dragons, though. It is only about 2 million years old, which is young for an island. There are many kinds of unique animals on the island, such as monkeys, deer, pigs, birds, buffalo, and the Komodo dragon. Komodo Island also has a beach with pink sand. This is only one of seven in the world. Whether you want to take a picture on a pink beach or see a giant lizard, Komodo Island has something for everyone.
